recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **Afterparty Signal** as a mobile-first browser-native Canvas game. Preserve the source mechanics exactly: a start overlay opens an active animated canvas; five visible character anchors can be tapped with a 60px hit radius; taps spawn short floating dialogue bubbles that drift and fade; the central focal character triggers a brief glitch/HUD mood change; empty-space taps create a small burst of five glitter/ripple particles; no score, win/loss, physics, or new progression rules are added.

The authored world is a hyper-stylized neon teen-drama private story. Violet is the focal identity-crisis protagonist, surrounded by classmates representing vulnerability, toxic romance, friendship, and late-night digital intimacy. The scene should read as a glittery melancholy afterparty/school-hallway memory with phone UI motifs, DM cards, pink/cyan/violet lighting, scanlines, and compact portrait HUD language. Use vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with procedural Canvas art and mobile-safe controls.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current Game Truth
- genre: Interactive canvas vignette / tap-to-reveal character chatter toy.
- objective: Start the scene, tap visible characters to spawn short dialogue bubbles, tap the focal character for a temporary glitch state, and tap empty space for ripple particles.
- input model: Start button uses normal click/tap; active play uses pointerdown on the canvas with a preserved 60px character hit radius and empty-space fallback.
- core loop: Continuous requestAnimationFrame canvas scene; static character anchors bob visually; pointer hits create chat bubbles that drift/fade; special focal tap shakes/tints the scene briefly.
- fail/friction state: No win/loss; friction is temporary emotional/glitch feedback and fading messages.

## Protected Mechanics
- Preserve start overlay -> active canvas flow, five tappable characters, tap radius, chat bubble lifetime/fade, special focal glitch, empty tap ripple, HUD status change, audio unlock by user gesture, and portrait-safe touch controls.

## Remix Blueprint
Euphoria neon teen-drama narrative. An Euphoria neon teen-drama narrative game with hyper-stylized nightlife, emotional chaos, identity crisis, romance toxicity, vulnerability, digital-age intimacy, and glittery melancholy with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The rebuilt public surface reframes the tap-to-chat toy as a neon afterparty private-story scene. Violet is the focal identity-crisis avatar; classmates orbit her as romance pressure, vulnerability, friendship, and digital-age intimacy. Mechanics remain tap/reveal/glitch/ripple; presentation, HUD, copy, character silhouettes, and background ownership are rebuilt.
